Subject: north depot downtime, the numbers for Tuesday

Hi Carla,

Thanks for the full walkthrough today. You said the north depot is where downtime hurts most, so I put the summary together around that. It's attached as one page for your CFO before Tuesday. The bracketed numbers are the ones I'll fill in with you, so tell me what you have on hand.

Could you send me your current north depot downtime hours per month, and roughly what an hour of a truck off the road costs you? That lets us put a real number on it.

Thanks,
[Your name]

---

ROI SUMMARY: Ridgeway Waste, north depot focus

The problem
- 120 trucks across 3 depots. North depot logs [X] unplanned off-road hours per month.
- Scheduling today: [spreadsheet / paper / other].

What Driftline covers
- Preventive maintenance scheduling in one place, so service comes up on time.
- Parts inventory, so repairs aren't waiting on parts.
- Technician assignment, so work goes to the right person.
- Driver app and DVIR forms, so inspections are logged in the field.

Estimated impact (north depot, first year)
- Downtime reduction assumed: [X]%, recovering [Y] hours per month.
- Value of recovered hours: [Y] hours x [$ per truck-hour] x 12 = [$].
- Driftline cost: [pricing tier], [N] trucks, [$ per year].
- Net first-year return: [$]. Payback in [N] months.

Assumptions
- [Downtime reduction rate, based on what the north depot has seen or what Ridgeway expects.]
- [Cost per truck-hour, from Ridgeway's own numbers.]

Proposed next step
- [Pilot at the north depot / 30-day trial / full rollout], starting [date].

Note: The notes don't include downtime hours, cost per hour, or the price, so I left those as placeholders instead of guessing. Once you send those, I can fill in the math and tighten the email.
